members.name: persuasion_strategy
members.instructions: In a charity-donation chat, a persuader tries to get the other person (persuadee) to donate to Save the Children. Tag the LAST persuader message (the one after 'Persuader message to tag:') with exactly one persuasion strategy / dialogue act, following the annotation scheme. Use the earlier chat only to understand what the message responds to. Tag the message itself, not the chat. Key rules: any question the persuader asks that is not a donation ask, a how-much question, a 'have you heard of Save the Children' question, or a personal question about the persuadee's kids/charity giving is task-related-inquiry (opinions, 'any questions?', 'Did you know...?' quizzes, even 'Where are you from?'). Statistics and descriptions of children's suffering are emotion-appeal, NOT logical-appeal. Any description or praise of Save the Children, or a bare website link, is credibility-appeal. The persuader's own giving, past or planned or matching, is self-modeling. personal-story and off-task are rare. Flat fillers like 'Yes.' 'Ok.' 'Indeed.' are other.

criteria.greeting: Hello/hi, 'How are you today?', 'I am doing well thank you', 'Glad you are doing well' - opening small talk about how each is doing.
criteria.acknowledgement: A reaction or agreement with what the persuadee just said: 'Absolutely.', 'I agree.', 'Me too.', 'ok, I understand that.', 'That makes sense', 'That's great to hear', agreeing/sympathising with their comment.
criteria.praise-user: Compliments or praise of the persuadee, esp. right after they commit or offer to donate: 'Great!', 'That's amazing!', 'You are so kind', 'People like you make the world better', 'I admire that'.
criteria.thank: Thanks the persuadee for their time or donation: 'Thank you for your donation', 'We appreciate your help'.
criteria.source-related-inquiry: Asks whether the persuadee knows / has heard of Save the Children or what they know about the organization: 'Have you heard of them?', 'Are you familiar with Save the Children?', 'What do you know about this organization?'
criteria.personal-related-inquiry: Asks about the persuadee's own life, spending habits or charity giving: 'How much money do you spend on candy?', 'Do you have children?', 'Do you donate to charities?', 'Which charities do you usually donate to?', 'Have you ever donated?', 'Are you involved in children's charity?'
criteria.task-related-inquiry: Catch-all for other persuader questions: asking opinions or feelings ('What do you think?', 'What is your opinion about children's charity?', 'Do you want some info?', 'Any questions?', 'Do you agree?'), 'Did you know...?' quizzes, even 'Where are you from?'. NOT direct donation asks.
criteria.proposition-of-donation: Any direct ask or invitation to donate (whether they will donate at all): 'Would you be willing to donate some of your payment?', 'Would you consider donating?', 'Donate some money maybe?', 'Is this an organization you would consider donating to?', 'Would you do it now?', 'Hey, do some good, give some money to kids.'
criteria.ask-donation-amount: Asks how much they will donate, or asks about a specific small figure as a question: 'How much would you like to give?', 'What amount would you feel comfortable donating?', 'Could you afford fifteen cents?', 'So you are donating $10, right?'
criteria.foot-in-the-door: Statement that even a small amount helps or costs little, or the persuader's own experience that a few dollars go far: 'Even a small donation makes a difference', 'Every little bit helps', '10 cents makes a difference', 'Pocket change is enough'.
criteria.donation-information: How donating works: payment mechanics ('deducted from your task payment', 'the research team will collect donations and send it to Save the Children'), amount range ('You can choose any amount from $0 to $2', 'It can be as much as you want'), statements suggesting an amount ('I was thinking a dollar to start with would be wonderful', 'I would suggest $20 a month'), payment methods.
criteria.emotion-appeal: Emotional language and facts/statistics about children's suffering: 'It makes me so sad', 'That horrifies me', '16,000 children die each day', 'children killed in Syria', 'Some of them are basically naked', 'weighing heavy on my heart', 'Children shouldn't be separated from their families', 'children dying who can benefit from the donation'.
criteria.logical-appeal: Reasoning that donating has an effect or is the right thing to do: moral arguments, comparisons, 'think of the little things you buy, donate instead', 'if everyone gave a nickel it is $16 million', 'children are our future so we must help'.
criteria.credibility-appeal: Describes or praises Save the Children or vouches for it: 'a trustable fund', 'top rated charity', 'international NGO that promotes children's rights', 'they work in health, education', '86% of funds go to programs', 'they helped children at the border', or a website link/URL.
criteria.self-modeling: The persuader's own giving of money, past, habitual or planned (NOT volunteering or general life remarks, which are other): 'I donate to them regularly', 'I will donate the same amount', 'I plan to match your donation', 'I usually put some money yearly', 'My charity of choice is Save the Children'.
criteria.personal-story: A story from the persuader's life or the story of a named child like Bruce (rare).
criteria.off-task: Chat completely unrelated to charity (very rare).
criteria.other: Flat fillers ('Yes.', 'Ok...', 'Indeed.', 'Yeah.', 'yes, you are correct'), vague remarks ('There are lots of opportunities'), check-ins like 'Does that sound ok to you?', persuader volunteering or life remarks ('I volunteer at a food bank'), closings ('Have a great night!', 'Take care'), remarks about the HIT, typo corrections ('sorry, typo'), replies about themselves ('I know I have.'), anything not fitting elsewhere.
